text:
Sam Rinzel spent October as a big, promising defenseman. He has spent November in a sentence with Bobby Orr, Borje Salming and Gordie Howe, the company he joined with five straight multi-assist games. It earned him the NHL's Third Star of the Week.

Our numbers say most of it is earned. He has 15 points in his last ten games, where his ice time alone would predict about six, and he is creating more of his own chances too. His ice time is up more than five minutes a night. Ten of his 18 points have come on the power play, which is why The Athletic's Mark Lazerus asked: "Did the Blackhawks power play fix Sam Rinzel? Or did Sam Rinzel fix the Blackhawks power play?"

Some will fade. Chicago has scored about ten more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, and his 2.4 points per 60 sit well above our talent range of 1.08 to 1.69. But Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 47% of his entries last season. The role looks real even if the pace isn't.
headline: Sam Rinzel has found the gear Chicago drafted
